messages:
simon: heads-up — saw a perf regression on the TP+fused-attn path when KV cache is enabled for long-context (>16k) workloads. latency p95 up ~18% across a 4xA100 cluster after yesterday's runtime change.

jess: ugh. any profile traces? nsys or perf?

simon: pasted a trimmed nsys timeline: 
```
GPU0: compute 0-120ms | allgather 120-180ms | idle 180-240ms
GPU1: allgather 0-60ms  | compute 60-180ms | allgather 180-220ms
```
looks like allgather spikes are interleaving with compute causing stalls.

kai: is this the new kernel-selector heuristic that prefers flash-attn when seq_len >= 4096?

simon: yes — kernel-selector chose flash-attn fused kernel for QKV-layout=TP-sharded. but Flash path ends up doing an extra QKV all-gather/transpose to assemble full heads before run, whereas the old non-fused path did local attention + reduce. that extra comm step scales poorly.

ria: can you drop the runtime flag `enable_fp16_fused_tp` and repro? want to know if it's selector or flash kernel impl.

simon: tried that — disabling fused kernel returns latency to baseline. so two candidates: selector misjudged net benefit, or fused kernel has inefficient comm pattern with KV-cache enabled.

jess: KV cache complicates things: we currently shard KV across TP dims to reduce memory. But for flash-attn we need contiguous KV per GPU for the fused fast path, so we force an allgather. That matches simon's observation.

kai: if stashing KV locally and using prefix-caching we could avoid frequent allgathers by doing partial local combines + async allreduce of deltas. Have we tried `--comm-strategy=async-reduce`?

simon: ran a micro-batch experiment with async reduce toggle: reduced p95 by ~7% but throughput variance increased. attaching microprof numbers (seq_len 8192, batch 2, tp=2): 
```
baseline fused: p95 420ms, stdev 30ms
async-reduce: p95 390ms, stdev 80ms
```

ria: variance spike is concerning for SLOs. maybe we can overlap KV packing with preceding compute and kick off NCCL allgather earlier. Is packing currently blocking?

jess: yes, packing happens in Python thread before CUDA kernel launch. we can move packing to a small CUDA kernel and issue comm earlier. Patch exists in draft PR #4523.

infra-bot: deploy bot: canary runtime v0.9.8-rc3 deployed to cluster "tp-canary-2" (4xA100) at 2026-03-18T10:12:34Z :rocket:

kai: PR #4523 looks promising. but kernel-selector also needs a quick heuristic change: if KV-cache enabled and tp_shard_kv=true, prefer non-fused for seq_len in [2048, 16384] unless latency-model predicts >10% win. currently selector's cost model underestimates comm cost.

simon: agree. i've got profiling traces for the selector cost-model showing missing the allgather term. i'll add a comm_cost_estimate in the predictor.

jess: another edge-case: flash-attn fails with `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` when head_dim % 64 != 0 on TP-sharded QKV layout; fallback occurs but selector wasn't notified, so we paid a compile+fallback penalty mid-deploy. saw this on a handful of customer runs.

ria: that's the old alignment bug — we should add a pre-flight kernel-compat check in the planner. cheap check, avoids runtime fallback.

kai: action items: (1) simon add comm_cost to selector predictor + rerun cost-sim, (2) jess land PR #4523 to pack KV on-GPU and kick off async allgather earlier, (3) ria add pre-flight kernel compatibility check to planner, (4) infra run canary with async-reduce off/on and report p95/stdev.

simon: i'll send a short perf-run config and target timeslots. want to test with varying micro-batch sizes (1,2,4) and tp=2/4.

jess: FYI — I also saw a tiny correctness drift in logits when we changed the fused kernel: mismatch at 1e-6 due to different FP accumulation order. added a diff-check to nightly evals.

simon: good catch. if accuracy drift ties to kernel reorder, we need a quant-regression gate in rollout pipeline.

infra-bot: perf-run scheduled: cluster tp-canary-2, start 2026-03-18T15:00Z, duration 2h.

ria: will pair-review the planner change. thanks all. :thumbsup:
